articles.title: Neither foam nor feathers - the perfect pillow for my neck and back is filled with buckwheat hulls
articles.summary: A small cotton tube stuffed with buckwheat hulls gave me firm, cool support that adapts to how I sleep. I thought I found the perfect pillow. Could these three unseat my favorite? Sign up for the Filter US newsletter, your weekly guide to buying fewer, better things.
body: I used to fight with my pillow all night. I would squash it, fold it, flip it over and shove my hand underneath for extra height. Still, I would wake with a tight neck that only my morning yoga practice could straighten out.

When I sleep, I start on my back, but end up sleeping on my side. Finding a pillow that doesn’t give me back or neck pain is a challenge, especially because I have wide shoulders and prefer a very firm bed. For me, a squishy pillow made little sense.

It took me years to realize that finding the right pillow depends on your sleeping position, body type and bed firmness. My journey led me beyond curved neck pillows, foam that stifled my ear and stacked pillows to make room for my shoulders when side sleeping and ended with a buckwheat hull pillow – the solution to all of my sleeping problems.

For more sleep recommendations, check out our guides to our favorite pillows from Coop, the sleep tech gadgets that actually work, the coziest PJs, or see why the Mzoo sleep mask is the secret to napping – anytime, anywhere.

articles.title: Take good care of your tailbone. I didn’t – and my derriere has never been the same since | Adrian Chiles
articles.summary: My coccyx still hurts from an extreme cycling challenge almost two decades ago. Is there anything it’s good for? ‘Welcome to middle age.” This is what my GP said to me 10 years ago when I asked her why I needed this pill or that. Being then just shy of 50, that hit home.
body: I interviewed Prof Alice Roberts this week. A writer, broadcaster, academic, anatomist, archaeologist and sometime medical doctor, she knows her bones, and no mistake. I noted with interest that her PhD thesis was titled “Rotator cuff disease in humans and apes: a palaeopathological and evolutionary perspective on shoulder pathology”. I’ve rarely felt so connected with my ancestors, so human, and indeed so ape-like. In an instant my shoulder pain became easier to bear, as I felt at one with a caveman wincing as he reached up to apply the finishing touches to some wall art.

After the radio show I was full of regret that I didn’t get time to ask her about another bone with which I’ve had my troubles: the coccyx. Mine has not been the same since I did some extreme cycling for Sport Relief with Alan Shearer 18 years ago. To this day, every so often if I sit wrong, I get a very nasty kind of electric shock shooting up from my derriere.

articles.title: Spermageddon, ‘greedy jobs’ and abject fear: why birth rates are plummeting – and why it matters
articles.summary: The author of Generation Maybe, Camilla Cavendish, explains the many reasons people are having fewer children, from dating apps to unaffordable housing and the climate crisis.
body: When I meet her in central London, Cavendish is tailored, self-possessed, you might even say poised, but very open – she never gives an opinion without asking yours, she talks very freely about her family and she is upfront about what she sees as her faults. Now 58, she started her career at McKinsey, the mega-management consultancy, having done PPE at Oxford at the same time as David Cameron, for whom she worked as policy director when he was in government and to whom she remains intensely loyal (every time his name comes up, we have a fight).

She’s now a baroness, but you can’t imagine her relishing her correct address – she wouldn’t like the pomposity. She’s an FT columnist and a fellow of Harvard Kennedy school, which specialises in public policy. This duality shows: in her writing and in conversation, she slips quite seamlessly between the academic and the journalistic. “What drives me,” she says of this book, “is the feeling that so many people are missing out. It’s not the economics, it’s the heartache.”

articles.title: Hard parties, cheap rents and horrible flats: how 90s art and fashion redefined British culture
articles.summary: An evocative new Tate Britain show captures an era when the UK’s newly flush creative industries teamed up with a generation of skint dreamers to bring the decade into vivid colour. Here is Kate Moss, with pink hair splayed across a pillow, her face scrubbed of makeup, her smile sweet and wonky.
body: These photos are old. They were taken a long time ago. But they’re young, too. They are curated by Edward Enninful for the Tate’s exhibition The 90s: Art and Fashion (Enninful worked at i-D in the 90s) and almost everyone involved is shiny and fresh. The models, whether professional or not, are mostly in their 20s, and the photographers are early in their careers. It gives the photos a youthful fizz, a verve. But the energy also comes from an understanding between photographer and subject. In many of the pictures you can feel the shared mischief, a “yes we’re serious about our ideas” but also a “look, we’re getting away with it!” delight.

Parties were plentiful. Aside from the club scene, magazines threw them, art galleries threw them, some random person that you met in a late-night drinking den said, “I know this place”, so you went. When you were out, you met artists, photographers, musicians, actors, writers, promoters, dealers, “entrepreneurs”. Often you had no idea what they did: I once walked into an office and realised that the esteemed head of design was the character with whom I’d spent a full-on all-nighter at Glastonbury a month before.

articles.title: Bloomingdale’s Raised a Glass to the CFDA/Vogue Fashion Fund Finalists
articles.summary: On Wednesday evening, the fourth floor of the Bloomingdale’s flagship gave a glimpse into the future of American fashion—one that looked pretty promising by all accounts.
body: The class of 2026 spans womenswear and menswear labels, as well as two jewelry lines: Aisling Camps, Amir Taghi, Terrence Zhou of Bad Binch TongTong, Emily Dawn Long, Jamie Haller, Julia Ferentinos of Juju Vera, Zane Li of Lii, George Inaki of Milamore, Claire Sullivan of Miss Claire Sullivan, and Zoe Gustavia Anna Whalen. As industry guests joined the designers for cocktails, they posed proudly beside their respective creations and talked people through their modus operandi.

“I love seeing everyone’s work on these mannequins—I’m imagining them on the floor in a few months time,” beamed Chloe Malle, head of editorial content at American Vogue. “From the work that the designers have on display here tonight, you can see how incredibly varied their references are. But what they share is a real singularity of vision and commitment to the craft, and I am so in awe of everything that they are doing.”

“Bloomingdale’s really loves to support emerging designers and give them a platform,” agreed Denise Magid, the retailer’s Chief Merchant and a member of this year’s selection committee, adding, it’s an honor to help share their “tremendous creativity” with prime real estate within the store.

articles.title: 11 Scenic Train Rides in the US Worth Booking for the Views Alone
articles.summary: From Amtrak routes along California’s coast to the wild beauty of the Alaska Railroad, the best way to see the vast natural beauty of the US is by train.
body: Every year, instead of flying home to southeastern Virginia, I always opt to take the train.

My journey typically starts in New York, winding down the Northeast Corridor before stopping in Washington, DC. While this busy stretch of track is far from the most scenic train ride in the US, there were still moments when I found my face pressed against the window—like near Havre de Grace, Maryland where the Susquehanna River widens—unable to look away. It was a reminder of how the joys of slow travel can sneak up on you, even in familiar places you may have traveled through countless times before.

articles.title: In the Rainforest of Chilean Patagonia, Pushing My Limits at a Trail Running Retreat
articles.summary: Eager to become a more intrepid runner, writer Maryann Wright ventures to the weather beaten trails of Chile's Los Ríos region—and expands her belief of what's possible.
body: It’s 3 a.m., zero degrees, and drizzling, and I’m standing in the middle of the Punucapa rainforest in the southern Los Ríos region of Chile, about to go for a run. Back home in my comfortable corner of south east London, with its mere four months of annual sunshine and warmth, I'd become desperate to not be a fair weather runner. But this now seems like a rather extreme approach to my New Year’s resolution to embrace running in the wet and cold.

I’m not alone: a canopy of evergreen, moss-covered trees, and a floor of giant Jurassic ferns envelop me along with 80 other runners, all awake and full of adrenaline at this unseemly hour. An Indigenous Mapuche singer’s voice rings out into the silence in an ancestral welcome chant; we are on his people’s land, and he wishes us safe travels as we scale the punishing mountains. Soon, though, it will be just me, my head torch, and the dancing mist as my warm breath rapidly condenses into the pitch black night.

articles.title: What You Need to Know About Walmart's 'Fall Deals' Sale
articles.summary: We may earn a commission from links on this page. Deal pricing and availability subject to change after time of publication. Amazon's Prime Big Deal Days promotion—think of it as October Prime Day—is typically one of the biggest sales of the fall, and every year, it prompts other retailers to…
body: Walmart Fall Deals is the answer to Amazon's October Prime Day sales, officially known as Prime Big Deal Days. It is both an in-store and online sale with deals on most things that Walmart sells (food being arguably the biggest omission). The sale happens every year around spring, summer, fall, and winter, revolving around Prime Day sales.

Walmart Fall Deals kicks off at midnight ET on Oct. 5 and runs through Oct. 11. For Walmart+ members, there is usually a pre-sale period where they can get deals before everyone else (last year it was five hours long).

You can always expect major retailers to have their own competitive sales around Amazon's October Prime Day. So far, Target has announced its sale, but we've yet to hear from Best Buy. As in previous years, the dates for these sales tend to start earlier, overlap, and run longer than October Prime Day. There are usually a couple of deals that are better than Amazon's Prime Day at each of the retailers too, so it behooves you to shop around if there's a particular item you want.

articles.title: Karlie Kloss and Wes Gordon Threw a 45th Anniversary Party for Carolina Herrera
articles.summary: If you thought the previously shuttered Mortimer’s restaurant on Lexington Avenue had magically reopened this week, you’d be partially correct, as the famed Upper East Side institution was rebranded as Herrera’s for one-night-only.
body: Despite showing his latest collection hours earlier, Gordon was refreshed and in high spirits. Holding court in the restaurant’s plush corner booth with Karlie Kloss and Aerin Lauder, he shared with Vogue how the establishment was always a favorite of Mrs. Herrera’s. With black and white balloons covering the ceiling, dark red flowers blooming around the venue, and silver streamers gleaming in the candlelight, the soirée certainly paid homage to the label’s sophisticated uptown DNA.

Gordon was joined by longtime Herrera muse Kloss, who closed the aforementioned runway and just marked a decade as the face of the brand’s Good Girl fragrance line. Dressed in a classic white shirt, black skirt, and matching pumps—a nod to Mrs. Herrera’s signature ensemble—Kloss also had the honor of blowing the candles out on the label’s 45th anniversary cake.

articles.title: The Best Early Prime Day Deals 2026, According to Vogue Editors
articles.summary: Prime Day returns this October! Here’s what Vogue editors think are the best early Prime Day deals 2026—from beauty to fashion and everything in between.
body: Mark your calendars: Just in time for the start of the holiday shopping season, Amazon’s next major savings event is coming October 6 and 7. Known as Prime Big Deal Days, the retailer’s fall counterpart to Prime Day is a 48-hour event that will offer Prime members discounts across fashion, beauty, tech, and more.

As someone who spends a lot of time online shopping (perils of the job), I’ve learned that my approach to Prime Day is less about filling my cart with things simply because they’re marked down and more about keeping tabs on the items I’ve already been eyeing. I use the event as an opportunity to restock some of my beauty favorites—Supergoop! sunscreen, Anastasia Beverly Hills brow gel—as well as wardrobe staples I go through every year, like white Hanes tees and Natori cotton underwear. And if there’s a big-ticket kitchen or home item I’ve been considering, I’ll check to see whether the sale brings the price down enough to finally invest.
